title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
venue: arXiv:2607.12227v4 (5 Oct 2026), preprint; Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington

selection.evidence: Cited by lee2026-rhi as the negative result ('automatic harness evolution fails to consistently outperform simple test-time scaling'). Chosen as the independent counterweight to the two Sakana records, from another group with code.

cost.compute_notes: 26-page PDF: body read in full (Secs 1-5, Tables 1-4), appendix not read. Code repo cloned (203 files, no per-task results). w01 ran in 39 s plus 20 s.

triggers: train test separation in agent search

claims.statement: On Terminal-Bench 2.1 without unit tests, automatic harness evolution (AHE) does not beat direct sampling on average (67.4 vs 68.2 pass@1) and falls below parallel sampling with self-selection (72.3); on GPT-5.4 it drops 75.3 -> 69.7.
claims.scope: 89 tasks, 2 runs each, K = 5 budget for every method, three models (Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini). AHE with its explore agent disabled, m = 1 rollout per task per harness.

quantities.name: same_procedure_replicate_difference
quantities.unit: pp: direct sampling in Table 2 minus Table 1, per model

our_assessment.why: The direction is credible and the design (matched K, same seed harness) is the right one. No intervals are given. The paper's own replicate of an identical procedure moves by up to 2.5 pp, so per-model differences of about 2 pp are not resolved. The GPT-5.4 drop (-5.6) and the parallel-sampling advantage (+4.1 on average) are larger than that floor. 'Fails to outperform' is supported. 'Self-feedback is noisy and compounds mistakes' is an interpretation.

claims.statement: With unit tests, harness evolution still trails test-time scaling: pass@1 69.7 vs parallel sampling 82.0; pass@5 79.0 vs sequential refinement 87.1. Its gains appear only when selecting among several attempts.

our_assessment.why: The gaps (12 pp at pass@1, 8 pp at pass@5) are well above the replicate floor. A clean matched-budget result.

claims.statement: Harness evolution fails to generalise: on 34 held-out tasks the evolved harness gains +1.2, 0.0 and -1.4 pp (average 0.0), which 'stands in sharp contrast' to its in-sample improvements and indicates overfitting to the search set.
claims.scope: 45 train / 10 validation / 34 test split of Terminal-Bench 2.1, 2 runs.

our_assessment.why: 'No gain on held-out' holds. A +5 pp per-model gain would be missed 5-25% of the time, depending on how deterministic tasks are (w01 B). 'Overfitting' does not hold: overfitting needs an in-sample gain to lose, and the in-sample pass@1 gains are -0.8 and +2.1, inside the replicate floor. The 'improvements on the same tasks' being contrasted are pass@5 or selection gains, not a better harness at pass@1. The supported reading is that the evolved harness does not help anywhere at pass@1; nothing shows a train/test gap.

claims.statement: In long-horizon games with rich feedback, task-specific harness evolution ('harness scaling') beats sequential refinement at matched budget: ARC-AGI-3 RHAE 43.3 -> 77.5 (Opus 4.8) and 21.1 -> 38.2 (GPT-5.6 Terra) when allowed to evolve skills and tools; +11% on EdgeBench games.
claims.scope: 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, 2,000-action budget, best score over the run; starting from the strong VISTA harness with memory evolution off.

our_assessment.why: Large effects, but single runs per game are implied and not stated, and the per-game scores swing 0-100 (e.g. tr87 11.8 -> 100). The comparison is to sequential refinement, not to parallel sampling. Not recomputed: no per-run logs.

instrument_checks.world: true harness gain +5 pp, task determinism calibrated to the paper's replicate
true gain +5 pp, Beta(conc 1.5) task heterogeneity

checked.how: clone; find -type f (203 files); search for result files
checked.result: Agent and evolve-agent code (nexau framework) only; no per-task outcomes, so no number in the paper can be recomputed.

open_questions: Do RHI's sonnet and opus gains survive a parallel-sampling baseline at equal cost (best-of-k with the same frontier judge)? RHI never ran it.
Is the identical 69.9 for Opus 4.6 direct sampling in Tables 1 and 2 a reused run? If so, the replicate floor is 2 pairs, not 3.
ARC-AGI-3: repeat runs per game -- how much of 43.3 -> 77.5 is one lucky trajectory on a few games?
